Two bytes, 0 and $A8, read at $871E and compared at $8734 with X = 0 in code not yet traced; purpose not established.

A +1/-1 wobble (0, 1, -1, 0), indexed by ($7B / 4) AND 3 at $8843 and added to $AB-$AF (code not yet traced).

Which equipment flag lets the player see a building's warning, by its stage bits 2-3: none, PK detector ($01), marshmallow sensor ($04), PK detector. Read at $7D74; without the flag the building shows as normal.
The state a building takes when its timer (the high nibble of $C8,x) runs out, by its current stage bits 2-3: $14, $1C, $F8, $1F. Read at $73EB.

Busting: base sprite shapes for sprites 0-3 ($25, $1F, $1F, $1F), plus the animation step $79, stored to $2B-$2E by $9A43; $87A7 reads the first.

Equipment shop: positions of the cargo slots in the car, 24 bytes per vehicle (offset from cargo_slot_base), read at $77B7 with the forklift stop $5F and $61; stored to $B0,y as a sprite target.
Equipment shop: 4 bytes per page ($5D x 4 + row, $783F), giving $61, the offset into a vehicle's cargo_slot_pos: page 1 0-3, page 2 0, 4-6, page 3 0, 7.
Items of cargo each vehicle carries: 5, 9, 11, 7. $78EA compares the count loaded ($62) and, when full, shows status message 7 (YOUR CAR IS LOADED TO CAPACITY).
Driving: the speed limit of each vehicle ($60, $70, $80, $A0), the cap on $1B at $80C5; the manual gives 75, 90, 110, 160 mph.
Equipment shop: the forklift's target x for the two sides, by bit 0 of the stop $5F ($28 or $4C, $777B); the last two bytes ($4C, $4C) are not read.
Equipment shop: x, y of the five shelf item sprites (x $14, y $52, $72, $92, $AB, $C2), copied to $A6-$AF and $B6-$BF at $770D.
Equipment shop: the last forklift stop on each page (9, 9, 1), compared with $5F at $78CB.

Equipment shop: the sprite shape on each shelf, 8 bytes per page, first 5 used ($76EA with Y = page x 8 + 4 down to page x 8): page 1 $33-$35 (detector, intensifier, sensor), page 2 $36, $38, $39 (bait, traps, vacuum), page 3 $3A (laser). Shape $37, item 4 ($600 in item_price, no flag), is on no page: an item that cannot be bought. Bytes 5-7 of each page are never read.

Eight bytes (0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 0, $20, $40) that repeat item_flag shifted by one entry. Not read in any simulator run, and no indexed read found reaches them (shelf_shapes stops at $AAC7); apparently unused.
'--CREDIT--' in screen codes, copied to row 0, columns 26-35 ($541A) by $739F and a row of dashes two rows below, when $5E is set.
Eight bytes ($02, $09, $10, $17, $10 x 4) with no reader found: not read in any simulator run, and no instruction addresses them. Purpose unknown.
Screen row start / 4 for rows 0-25 (row x 10). The typewriter text printer at $9CB7 shifts it left twice into $5400 + row x 40 for the character and $D800 + row x 40 for its colour.
Per vehicle: high byte of its picture data, $0200, $0500, $0800, $0B00, read at $7669 (low bytes in car_picture_lo).
Per vehicle: low byte of the picture address (all 0), read at $7670.

First character code of each of the 12 columns of a 12 x 16 character picture window ($40, $50 ... $F0): $35FC fills each column with 16 consecutive codes from here, starting at screen $54B2, colour 8. Drawn by the routine at $35E6, called from the vehicle page ($75D2) and $76BF.

Text page 1: the letterhead (GHOSTBUSTERS / FOR PROFESSIONAL / PARANORMAL / INVESTIGATIONS / AND ELIMINATIONS / -WE'RE READY TO BELIEVE YOU-) and the name prompt ending LAST,FIRST:. Pages are PETSCII typed out by $72EA and $9C8F: $0D starts a new line, a byte $80-$BF moves to column (byte AND $3F), $00 prints nothing (a pause), $FF ends the page.

Text page 3, after N: IN THAT CASE, WELCOME TO YOUR NEW BUSINESS, three $00 pauses, then the bank's $10000 advance and GOOD LUCK.

The 36 characters PRESS SPACE BAR TO VIEW CAR OPTIONS. inside page 8, also copied straight to row 17 ($5749) by $75DF when the options are redrawn.
The 36 characters PRESS 1,2,3 OR 4 TO PURCHASE CAR. inside page 8, copied to row 18 ($5771) by $75E8.
Text page 9, shop page 1: MONITORING EQUIPMENT with the PK energy detector $400, image intensifier $800, marshmallow sensor $800, two empty shelf lines, and the forklift instructions.
Text page 10, shop page 2: CAPTURE EQUIPMENT, ghost bait $400, TRAPS -REQUIRED- $600, ghost vacuum $500.
Text page 11, shop page 3: STORAGE EQUIPMENT, portable laser confinement system $8000.

Text page 16: YOU MADE MORE MONEY THAN YOU STARTED WITH, SO THE BANK WILL RAISE YOUR CREDIT LIMIT TO (the amount follows).
Text page 17: YOUR NEW ACCOUNT NUMBER IS (the number follows).
Text page 18: . WRITE THIS NUMBER DOWN FOR FUTURE PLAY.
Text page 24: CONGRATULATIONS( THANKS TO YOU, - the character '(' is drawn as an exclamation mark by the game's character set ($5800 + $28 x 8).
Text page 25, the winning ending: THE PORTAL TO THE SPIRIT WORLD HAS BEEN CLOSED. YOU EARN A $5000 REWARD FROM THE CITY. ALSO,
Text page 26: STARTING BALANCE:
Text page 27: ENDING BALANCE:

Addresses of the 28 text pages, by page number x 2, read at $9BFD/$9C02 by $9BEE (A = page, bit 7 set also sets $EA76) into the typewriter pointer $4E/$4F. Page 0 is at $EA14 and page 12 at $EB00 (built in RAM at run time), pages 20-23 are the car options at $38DE-$39B6, page 19 is the empty page at $B3A9, the rest are in this range.
High bytes of the text_page_ptrs words, read as $B36E,x at $9C02.
Text page number of each vehicle's options (20-23), read at $7609 and passed to $9BEE when SPACE steps through the cars.
Text page 19: a lone $FF, a page that ends at once.
'GHQ' in screen codes, written under the GHQ block of the city map ($572E) by $7B60.

Two joystick readings made up by the game, $07 (right) and $0B (left); $85BF reads the first and third (X = 2, 0), EORs them with $0C to swap left and right when needed and ORs in the player's $33 before moving the men ($9AF1, code not yet traced). The middle byte is not read.
Status message 9: GO TO ZUUL( SNEAK PAST THE MARSHMALLOW MAN AND CLOSE THE PORTAL... , shown by $99CC through status_msg_lo/hi; '(' is drawn as '!'.
Low bytes of the ten status-line messages shown by $99CC (X = message): $3A16, $3A40, $3A78, $3A89, $3AB0, $3AC5, $3B21, $3B5F, $3B80 and txt_go_to_zuul.
High bytes of the ten status-line message addresses, read at $99D5.

The run-length packed sprite shapes: the cold start's unpacker at $610B reads from here to $BFF7 and writes 3,800 bytes to $4000-$4ED7, sprite shapes 0-59 (shape n at $4000 + n x 64). A byte $11 is followed by a count of zero bytes to write (0 meaning 256); every other byte is copied. Shape 59 gets only its first 8 rows.
Second kilobyte of packed_sprites ($B408-$BFF7): the run-length stream of the sprite shapes continues.
Third part of packed_sprites, to $BFF7 where the unpacker's end test at $610D stops.

Eight bytes after the end of packed_sprites that the unpacker never reads (it stops when the source reaches $BFF8). They continue shape 59's pattern (FF FF F8, FF FF F8, F8 6D), so the stream was cut short or this is leftover; nothing else reads them.

The conversion's hand-over to the game, called once by the stub at $033C after the one-file load (orientation.md): SEI; masks every CIA 1 and CIA 2 interrupt ($7F to $DC0D and $DD0D) and reads both interrupt registers to clear what is pending; copies the 256 bytes at $C830 to $0300-$03FF and zeroes $0200-$02FF, putting back the two pages the load had to overwrite; then JMP $6000, the game's cold start, never returning. Nothing in the game calls it (no instruction names $C800).
Fourteen $FF bytes between oneload_handover and its page image; no instruction names them and no simulator run reads them. Filler.

Page image copied to $0300-$03FF by oneload_handover ($C811): $0300-$0313 zero, $0314/$0315 = $0A00, $0316/$0317 = $2F0B, $0318/$0319 = $352D, then 230 bytes that look like graphics (runs of $AA, $0F, $03, $BA...). It is what the conversion found in that page. Nothing in the game uses it: no instruction names $0300-$03FF, the IRQ and NMI go through $FFFE/$FFFA with the KERNAL banked out, and the simulator's read maps (title to the end of a game) show no read of $0300-$03FF.

A turbo tape loader left in memory, never executed in this image: no instruction jumps to $CE00-$CED5 (only $CF80, itself never reached) and the simulator never ran it. What it would do: $00 = $2F, $01 = $06 (cassette motor on), screen off ($D011 = $0B), NMI vector $0318 = $CEC1 (RESTORE while loading wipes memory), CIA 2 timer A latch $0118; syncs on 256 one-bits then a zero and the byte $33; reads a 2-byte start address into the store at $CE5B (self-modified), a 2-byte end address into $CED8/$CED9, then data bytes to the end address (exclusive) with an XOR checksum in $CED7; a matching checksum byte calls the KERNAL at $FC93, $FDA3 (IOINIT) and $FD15, CLI and returns; a mismatch goes to tape_load_fail ($CEC1). Which program this loader originally fetched is not known.
store address, self-modified from the block header at $CE43/$CE49 and stepped at $CE8B/$CE93

Operand of the dead loader's STA $BFFF at $CE5B, the load address: written from the header at $CE43, compared with the end address at $CE64, and stepped at $CE8B. The loop from here stores each byte, updates the checksum, and stops when this address reaches tape_end_address.
High byte of the dead loader's store address (header byte 2, $CE49), stepped at $CE93 when the low byte wraps, compared at $CE6C.
Part of the dead tape loader: reads 8 bits, most significant first, through tape_read_bit into $CED6 and returns the byte in A.

Part of the dead tape loader: waits for a pulse on the cassette read line (CIA 1 interrupt flag bit 4, the FLAG input, in $DC0D), then shifts CIA 2's timer A underflow flag (bit 0 of $DD0D) into the carry: 1 when more than $0118 cycles have passed since the previous pulse, a long pulse; restarts the timer ($DD0E = $11) and flips the border colour (EOR 5) for the familiar loading stripes.

Part of the dead tape loader, reached on a checksum mismatch and installed as the NMI (RESTORE) handler at $CE10: stores $02 into every byte from $0202 upward (pointer $9E/$9F) flashing the border, then JMP $FCE2 (the KERNAL's reset). The fill reaches its own loop at $CEC7 on the way, and $02 is a JAM opcode, so in practice it would stop the processor before the reset. An anti-tamper wipe.
Dead tape loader variable: the byte being assembled by tape_read_byte ($CE9E ROL, $CEA4 read).
Dead tape loader variable: XOR of the data bytes loaded (cleared at $CE29, updated at $CE5E-$CE61, compared with the block's last byte at $CE78).
Dead tape loader variable, 2 bytes: the block's end address from its header ($CE4F, $CE55), compared with the store address at $CE67/$CE6F.
High byte of tape_end_address (header byte 4, written at $CE55, compared at $CE6F).

Four calls never executed and named by no instruction: JSR $CE00 (tape_turbo_loader), JSR $0A00, JSR $CE00, JSR $0E00, then a $00 byte (BRK): load a block and run it, twice. Together with the $0A00 IRQ vector in page3_image it looks like the remains of the original tape loading sequence; what $0A00 and $0E00 held then is not known (in this image they are part of the game).

Six pages holding characters $40-$FF of the character set at $5A00-$5FFF, that is the car picture with the bought equipment painted in: saved there when leaving the shop (st10_map_setup, $7AC8 through $9D96) and copied back to $5A00 at the start of each drive ($8007-$8027), because the map's character set replaces it in between. Runtime storage: the image's bytes here are only the machine's power-on pattern.
Second part of car_charset_save ($E000-$E5FF): its pages 5 and 6, characters $C0-$FF of the saved car picture.

256-byte table built by cold_start ($6074-$6088): for each byte, every multicolour pixel pair with either bit set made %11, so AND with it keeps a shape's pixels and AND with its inverse clears the background under them. Read by shop_paint_item_in_car ($79EE) to cut the item's shape into the car picture.

256-byte table built by cold_start ($606C): each byte with its four 2-bit pixels in reverse order, a left-right mirror of multicolour graphics. Read by build_mirrored_sprites ($6156-$6183) for the sprites that face both ways and by build_car_charset ($76A2) for the car's right half.

92 bytes: the carried item's sprite shape shifted right to its pixel position in the car, 4 bytes per row for 23 rows, written by shop_paint_item_in_car ($79CA-$79DC) and read back at $79EA/$79F7 to paint it into the car's characters. The simulator saw rows 0-20 read ($E800-$E853); $E854-$E85B are written only.

Not a variable: frame_ticker_scroll reads $E8D8,X with X from 40 up ($723A, $7257), which is ticker_buffer ($E900) + X - 40, the text window whose right edge is at $4B. No instruction reads or writes $E85C-$E8FF itself; in the image it is the power-on pattern.

Where frame_status_report writes the number of men left into the report text in ticker_buffer ($71F3, $E935,X, X = report length less $43).
Not a variable: frame_line_input ($738D) and input_add_char ($9C8A) store at $E9FF + $50, and $50 starts at 1, so the typed line begins at line_input_buffer ($EA00); nothing writes $E9FF itself.

The typed line of the interview and shop (name, yes/no, account number, vehicle number), PETSCII ended by 0: cleared for 20 bytes by st00_interview_start ($74AF), filled by input_add_char ($9C8A) and frame_line_input ($738D, the 0), read by st01_name_entered (20 bytes to $EAB3), st02_account_answer ($74D8), st0B_vehicle_choice ($7625) and account_parse_digits ($9D06). The length is limited only by the cursor column (below $25), so a long line can run past $EA13 into text_buffer.

20-byte text buffer, ended by $FF, printed as message $80/0 through select_message: the balance as text (money_to_text $9D24, bytes_to_digits $9D51, blank_leading_zeros $9D74, trim_leading_spaces $9063), the name as FIRST LAST (build_first_last_name $9B90, which clears all of $EA14-$EA27) and the PK and balance line (frame_pk_balance_line $72B1).
Offset 1 of text_buffer: blank_leading_zeros reads $EA15,X ($9D76) and money_to_text writes digits from $EA15 ($9D49).
Offset 3 of text_buffer: money_to_text writes the $FF end mark at $EA17,Y ($9D40, Y = 7, so at $EA1E).

30 bytes, one per map piece: the building shape drawn there, 0 for none. Set by init_game_vars_n ($9036) and at $89D3; read by st11_draw_map's draw_map_building_row ($9611), frame_spawn_haunts ($7449), map_fire_select ($7EC5) and pk_add_hundreds_carry ($98C5) to pick a building. Index 10 is Zuul and $11 GHQ (per those routines).

Second byte of sprite 0's saved position in map_sprite_pos_save (as $A1), written at $7BAF, $7D2F and $9878.

Second byte of each of sprites 2 and 3's saved positions (as $A5/$A7), written at $7C02.

Sprites 6-7's half of the Roamers' slot at $EA4E: restore_sprites_4_7 copies $EA52-$EA55 to $BC-$BF ($9844).

16 bytes, a copy of the map sprites' targets $B0-$BF (two bytes per sprite): from $37C3 at st10_map_setup ($7AA7) and reset_sprite_home ($9882); the logo's own position at map_building_under_logo ($7D28/$7D32); compared with the positions by st12_city_map ($7BB7/$7BBE) to see a Roamer arrive; restored into $B0 by st11_draw_map ($7B9B).
Second byte of sprite 0's saved target in map_sprite_target_save, written at $7D32 and $988C, compared at $7BBE.

Saved targets of sprites 2 and 3 within map_sprite_target_save: set with the targets $B4-$B7 by st12_city_map ($7C1F, sending them to Zuul) and by map_gatekeepers_wander ($7E3E, the next street crossing).
Second byte of each of sprites 2 and 3's saved targets, set at $7C27 and $7E4F.
Sprites 4-7's saved targets within map_sprite_target_save: $8A1D copies these 8 bytes back into $B8-$BF (the Roamers' targets) and returns to the map, state $12.
Sing-along ball: X position, low byte (bit 8 in ball_x_high $EA68); stepped by the hop's speed in singalong_ball_step ($9251, $9267), wraps to 0 past $157, zeroed by singalong_ball_reset ($929E).
Sing-along ball: Y position, moved by the 16-step bounce table at $8EA7 ($9239-$923C); $BA after singalong_ball_reset ($92A3).
Sing-along ball: bit 8 of the X position (with ball_x), ORed into the sprite X high bits for sprites 0 and 1 ($9283); zeroed by singalong_ball_reset.

Sing-along ball: pointer to the next byte of the hop script at $92BC, low byte here and high byte at $EA6A; stepped at $9215/$921A, set by singalong_ball_reset ($92B3/$92B8), sticks on the last byte ($93E1).
High byte of ball_script_ptr (the hop script pointer), stepped at $921A when the low byte wraps.
Sing-along ball: step 0-15 within the current hop, the index into the bounce table ($91D6); a new script byte is read when it is 0. Zeroed by singalong_ball_reset.
Sing-along ball: X speed for the current hop, the script byte with bit 6 cleared ($9212), added to ball_x each step ($924E).
singalong_ball_step's saved A, X and Y ($EA6D, $EA6F, $EA6E: stored at $91C8-$91CE, restored at $9292-$9298). $EA70 after them is named by no instruction and never touched in the simulator: unused.
singalong_ball_step's saved Y ($91CE, restored at $9298).
singalong_ball_step's saved X ($91CB, restored at $9295). The byte after it, $EA70, is unused.
Sing-along ball: hops still to wait in place, from a script byte of $80 or more (AND $7F, $920D); counted down at $91DB; zeroed by singalong_ball_reset ($92AE).

Scratch byte with two users: pk_add_hundreds_carry keeps the PK thousands digit (high nibble of $5B) before the addition in it ($989C) to see it change ($98A8), and saves X in it while picking a building ($98B1/$98DD); $861B-$8629 use it as a count of 64 raster interrupts, calling $9080 on each.

$FF on a PAL machine, $00 on NTSC: set by draw_title_screen ($62BD) from the last raster line; read by title_frame_work ($6338) and the raster IRQ ($8EE0) to run the tune's tick twice in one frame of eight on PAL.

pk_add_hundreds_carry's search index when PK reaches a new thousand at 5000 or more: starts at the random byte $06 ($98B6) and is incremented ($98CA) until map_slot_table holds a building at (index AND $0F, at least 4) that is not Zuul (10).
The voice music_play is working on, 0-2 ($93F6); music_voice3_busy ($9599) compares it with 2 so that the music leaves SID voice 3 to the sound effects while $98 is set.
Text colour flag of the current message: select_message sets 1 when bit 7 of the message number is set, else 0 ($9BF6); frame_type_message copies it to $48, the colour it prints with ($72E3).
Busting-scene flag, meaning not settled: 1 at $8A7C (the routine at $8A6A that also places sprites through $AA/$AB and $BA/$BB), $FF at $8AC2 after a man is lost, 0 at $8B58; tested at $8B1F.
Busting-scene counter: 2 at $8A5E; $8AE1 decrements it together with the men-left count $3D; $8B0B branches away when it is 0. Its partner is $EA79.
Busting-scene counter: 2 at $8A61; $8AB2 decrements it with the men-left count $3D and then plays speech phrase 3 ($8AB9); $8B10 branches away when it is 0. Its partner is $EA78.

Flag that makes two points of the play code speak: set to 1 at $86D2 and to $3B at $8C80, cleared at $8658, $8C8B and $8CFB; when non-zero, $8744 plays speech phrase 2 (just after adding 300 PK at $873F) and $8D18 plays phrase 3.

Sound-effect interpreter on SID voice 3 ($3BE9 on): the command byte just read from the effect's data ($3C34); its low nibble picks the handler from the tables at $3D83/$3D92 ($3C3C), and handlers read it back ($3C5B, $3CC5).
Sound-effect interpreter: X saved while fetching the next data byte through ($E7) ($3C61/$3C6E).

Sound-effect interpreter: the voice 3 control value with the gate bit clear ($3D0B, from the table at $3D74), written to $D412 to release the note when the duration reaches the release point ($3BFA) and with the gate set to start one ($3C81). Zeroed when an effect starts ($3D3F).

Sound-effect interpreter: a frequency wobble; each tick it is negated and added to the current frequency into $D40F ($3C06-$3C17), so the pitch alternates up and down. Set from a command's high nibble ($3CE4), zeroed when an effect starts ($3D42).

Sound-effect interpreter: repeat counter of a loop command ($3CCC): decremented at $3CCF, and while it is not 0 the data pointer ($E7) is moved back by the byte that follows. Set from a command's high nibble ($3CEC).
Sound-effect interpreter: the duration value at which the note's gate is released ($3BF5 compares sfx_duration with it); $FF (never) when an effect starts ($3D4B).

Sound-effect interpreter: ticks left in the current step, counted down each tick ($3BED); at 0 the next command is read ($3C03). Set from the table at $3D5C by a command's high nibble ($3C7A), 1 when an effect starts ($3D2C), 0 to stop ($3BE3, $3C53).

The value last written to $D418 (volume and filter mode) by music_play ($9483), kept so that it can be put back after the RUN/STOP pause silences the SID (frame_pause_key $70CE) and after speech ($8E39), and by frame_type_message ($730B-$7314).

Sound-effect interpreter: voice 3's frequency high byte ($D40F), set from the note table at $3DFA ($3CA0), moved by sweeps ($3C21/$3C27), relative steps ($3D1A) and the wobble ($3C14). $EA85 after it is named by no instruction: unused.

Sound-effect interpreter: frequency sweep direction, positive = up one step per tick, negative = down ($3C1A-$3C27); set by a command ($3CC8), zeroed when an effect starts ($3D45). $EA85 after it is named by no instruction and never touched in the simulator.
Sound-effect interpreter: the note number of the last note command ($3C90), the index into the frequency tables $3E5A/$3DFA; written only.

Set to 0 by draw_title_screen ($62D4) and read by nothing (no instruction names it, and no simulator run reads it). The disassembler's KERNAL name for $EA87 (scan keyboard) does not apply: here it is RAM.
A flag with no effect: 0 at $877E, 1 at $87C6, and the only read, LDA $EA88 / BEQ $8837 at $8832, branches to the next instruction either way. A left-over.
Sing-along ball: the script byte just read ($91F1), kept so that BIT can test its bit 6 ($91F5).
40 bytes: the screen row at $57C0 (row 22 of the $5400 screen), saved and blanked by the speech call $8DB9 on the title ($8DDE-$8DE7) while speech plays, and put back afterwards ($8E6A-$8E6F).
The function key that started the game: $20 for F1, $28 for F3 (title_frame_work $639F); zeroed by nmi_restore_handler ($6433); read by st00_interview_start ($747E) to skip the interview on F3.

The player's name as typed (LAST,FIRST), 20 bytes of PETSCII padded with zeros, copied from line_input_buffer by st01_name_entered ($74C0); summed by account_name_sum ($91BC) for the account number's check, and turned into FIRST LAST by build_first_last_name ($9BA3-$9BD0). It survives RESTORE, which is what lets F3 reuse it.

The account number, 4 bytes, one octal digit in each nibble: filled from the typed digits by st03_account_number ($750E-$751D) or by account_encode ($9114-$9149) at a win; read by account_decode ($915F) and printed at the end of a winning game ($8CC9-$8CD8). $EAC7 is the lowest byte.
Second byte of account_digits (written at $7513 and $9117, shifted at $912D/$9147, printed at $8CCE).
Third byte of account_digits (written at $7518 and $911A, shifted at $912A/$9144, printed at $8CD3).
Fourth and highest byte of account_digits (written at $751D and $911D, shifted at $9127/$9141, printed at $8CD8); account_decode reads its high nibble first.

121 bytes that cold_start fills with 120 spaces ($20) and an $FF end mark ($60E9-$60F7), the shape of a text buffer; no other instruction names $EB00-$EB78, and none of the simulator runs (title, interview, shop, map, drive, bust, Zuul, the winning ending) reads it. Initialised but unused in this version.
